summary: Alander Mountain (MA) tower built 1928 by Taconic State Park Commission; moved to Washburn Mtn in 1933 and to Beebe Hill State Forest, NY, in 1963 (sources differ on the year).

facts.status_note: Removed from Alander Mountain in 1930; the tower now stands at Beebe Hill State Forest, NY, where sources disagree on its current condition

access.note: Beebe Hill State Forest, where the moved tower stands, is public state land with trails; no source says the tower itself may be climbed. The Alander Mountain site is gone and no access is described there.

visit.trail_note: A main trail in Beebe Hill State Forest passes the tower; a lean-to near the trail is open for public use

events.note: Taconic State Park Commission erected a 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower on Alander Mtn. to detect fires on park land
The area at Alander Mtn. burned; the 1930 report to the NY Legislature credited the tower with 24 fires while the Park Commission ran it
Landowner asked for removal (register); the lease ended and the tower was dismantled and stored (register: High Falls facility; hobbyist page: park storage area until 1932)
Re-erected on Washburn Mountain in Columbia County, NY, inside park boundaries
Forest Fire Control took over operation at Washburn about 1935; operated there until 1963
November 1963: dismantled by Forest Rangers, flown by helicopter to Beebe Hill and re-erected. The hobbyist page and Wikipedia give 1964
Last operated at Beebe Hill; closed in 1987
Local residents, the Forest Fire Lookout Association and NYSDEC began efforts to restore the tower and establish hiking access
Wikipedia: as of late 2024 the Beebe Hill tower was deemed unsafe
As of 2025 the Beebe Hill tower was recently restored; wooden stairs replaced with metal

corrections.why: Alander Mt is the mountain's name, not an agency. The register says the Taconic State Park Commission erected the tower in 1928.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives November 1963 for the move to Beebe Hill. The hobbyist page and Wikipedia say 1964. The story gives the register's date and notes the other.

Wikipedia says the tower was deemed unsafe as of late 2024. The register says it was recently restored as of 2025. The hobbyist page says it has been restored and is open to the public. The story reports all three and does not pick one.
The register says the Park re-erected the tower on Washburn Mountain. The hobbyist page says the Conservation Department did. Both give 1933.

The brief's FFLOS coordinates (42.0925, -73.504444) match the register's own page (N 42.092500, W 073.504444). The second coordinate pair in the brief's conflict list (42.08759, -73.50512) does not appear on any page I read.

notes_for_editor: The brief's agency 'Alander Mt' is a mountain name and is proposed for correction. The access 'public' fact describes Beebe Hill State Forest, where the moved tower stands, not the Alander Mountain site; an editor may want a narrower note. The main open question is the tower's condition today: Wikipedia (late 2024, unsafe), the register (2025, restored) and the hobbyist page (restored, open) disagree. The register links beebehill.info; check it or NY DEC before publishing a 'today' claim. Elevation: the brief's 653.8 m matches the register's 2,145 ft (654 m); the hobbyist page gives the summit as 2240 ft and is not used. A search snippet from a Forest Fire Lookout Association Massachusetts chapter Facebook post gave 1932 for the Washburn re-erection; the page was not opened, so the story does not use it.
